summary: Redwood AE/SE demo of rate-limiting, quotas, and org/project key model for multi-tenant controls. Focus on how to enforce org-level quotas, project-scoped API keys, per-key rate limits, burst behavior, monitoring/alerts in Console, and Optimize suggestions for batching/caching. Customer is evaluating for a pilot; security and SSO questions noted.
topics: Optimize recommendations for token cost reduction
Security: SSO, RBAC, KMS, audit logs
transcript:
[00:00:00] Liam (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Liam from Redwood, AE. With me is Nadia and Samir from the solutions team. Today we'll walk through how rate limits, quotas, and org/project keys work in the Console and API.
[00:00:12] Dr. Karen Li: Hi Liam, thanks. Quick context — we're looking at using Redwood for in-product summarization across multiple business units, need strong multi-tenant controls and per-tenant quotas.
[00:00:25] Mike (CTO): Also security team will need audit logs and SSO integration details.
[00:00:30] Liam: Great, that's exactly what we'll cover. Nadia, take it away for the demo?
[00:00:35] Nadia (SE): Sure, I'll share my screen. Bear with me if the screen reader picks up some things oddly — we've had that with Fireflies before. Okay first slide shows the concept: org-level defaults, project-level overrides, and per-key limits.
[00:00:50] Nadia (SE): So, typical setup — you create an Organization in Redwood, add Projects for each product/team, and create API keys scoped to a Project. Keys can be project-scoped or org-scoped depending on how you want to isolate traffic.
[00:01:05] Priya (Platform Eng): Quick Q — can a single key be limited across multiple projects? We have services that talk to multiple backends.
[00:01:12] Nadia (SE): You can issue an org-scoped key that inherits org-level quotas, or issue project keys per project. Org-scoped keys are useful for shared infra; project keys give per-project billing and quotas. We do have token-based scoping for request tagging too.
[00:01:28] Samir (Solutions Eng): One note: there's not a nested policy system like IAM policies per request today — it's simpler scoping: org vs project, and keys can be RBAC-tagged in the Console.
[00:01:39] Jorge (Security): How do you enforce rate limits? Per-second? Per-minute? Any leaky-bucket behavior?
[00:01:44] Nadia (SE): We support per-key and per-project rate limits with both per-second and per-minute windows. By default we set soft quotas at the org level (for example 200 requests/min and 60k tokens/min) and you can override on a project or a key. We use a token-bucket style algorithm with configurable burst capacity so short spikes are allowed up to a burst limit.
[00:02:03] Priya: And if we exceed quota, what's the failure mode? 429? Queuing?
[00:02:08] Nadia: If you exceed hard quota you'll get 429 with a Retry-After header. For hosted customers we offer graceful fallback policies — e.g., automatic downgrade to a smaller model or fall back to a cached response — that's configurable in route policies. For Dedicated customers you can configure reserved capacity and burst credits to avoid 429s.
[00:02:25] Mike: How are tokens counted across streaming responses? We stream tokens and count them; the console shows token usage in near real-time.
[00:02:33] Liam: Important point — usage metering is per-request and per-token, and quotas can be set as requests-per-second or tokens-per-minute. Customers commonly set both to protect comping loops and runaway prompting.
[00:02:44] [00:03:00] Nadia: Switching to Console — here's the Quotas page. You can view org defaults, add project overrides, and create key-level limits. I'm creating a new project key now, scope: "patient-summaries-prod", setting limit: 30 requests/min, 15k tokens/min, burst 60 for 30s.
[00:03:20] Priya: Can we have separate quotas for embedding calls vs generation?
[00:03:24] Nadia: Yes, we support per-route and per-model quotas; route-level quotas are useful to separate embeddings from chat/generation. You can also tag keys and create policies that apply to tags.
[00:03:36] Samir: We also have metrics on cost per-route so you can see token-cost breakdown and set alerts if a route's spend exceeds thresholds.
[00:03:46] Jorge: About audit logs — do they show which key triggered what request? Retention?
[00:03:50] Nadia: Audit logs include key id, project, model used, and response status. Retention depends on plan: hosted default 90 days, enterprise options longer. Logs can be shipped to your S3 or Splunk for long-term retention.
[00:04:07] Mike: For compliance, we need KMS integration for customer-managed keys.
[00:04:11] Liam: We support KMS for encryption at rest and HSM options for Private deployments. We'll attach the security docs after.
[00:04:17] [00:04:30] Nadia: Back to API — headers you get back on rate-limited responses: x-rate-limit-remaining, x-rate-limit-reset, and Retry-After. We also expose them for embedding and streaming endpoints.
[00:04:43] Priya: Can we set different limits for internal vs external traffic? For example internal backends can have higher throughput.
[00:04:50] Nadia: Yes, use org-scoped keys for internal infra with higher quotas, and project-scoped keys for customer-facing flows. You can also set per-key metadata tags to indicate internal/external and create policies accordingly.
[00:05:05] Liam: Quick interjection — this is where Redwood Optimize can help. It analyzes your traffic patterns and suggests batching, caching prefixes, and model-quantization profiles to lower token cost and recommended quotas.
[00:05:18] Dr. Karen Li: Can Optimize automatically suggest different quotas based on observed peak windows?
[00:05:22] Samir: It gives recommended quota ranges and identifies hot routes and sequences with high prefix overlap — we surface suggestions in Console and as a downloadable report for the ops team. It won't auto-change quotas without approval.
[00:05:35] [00:05:50] Nadia: Demoing alerts — you can create alerts on quota usage percentage, cost spikes, or error-rate. Alerts support email, Slack, and webhook sinks.
[00:05:59] Jorge: What about per-customer billing? We need per-tenant chargeback.
[00:06:04] Nadia: Project-level metrics feed billing exports. We have CSV/BigQuery/S3 export for per-project cost breakdown so chargeback is straightforward.
[00:06:12] Priya: Is there throttling per-user inside a project? Like per-tenant within a single project?
[00:06:18] Nadia: Not as a first-class primitive — we recommend issuing separate project keys per tenant for strict isolation. Alternatively tag requests with a tenant id and use application-layer throttling plus per-route quotas.
[00:06:31] Liam: For your use case — patient summaries across units — a pattern many customers use is: org-scoped infra keys for background workers, project-per-product/team keys for per-tenant billing, and then issue customer-scoped keys for high-sensitivity tenants if strict isolation is required.
[00:06:47] [00:07:00] Mike: Can we rotate keys automatically?
[00:07:03] Nadia: Yes, keys can be rotated via the API and Console. You can create short-lived keys and integrate with your secrets manager. There's an API to create ephemeral keys for CI/CD use cases.
[00:07:12] Priya: How does the system handle region routing? We have EU data residency needs.
[00:07:17] Samir: We support region routing policies — you can pin projects to a region. Quotas and metrics are per-region; if traffic routes cross regions you'll see aggregated and per-region views.
[00:07:30] [00:07:45] Liam: Let's walk through a failure scenario: if a project exceeds bursts and hits hard quota, the Console shows spike, alert fires, and you can either temporarily raise the quota (if enterprise) or redirect traffic to a fallback model. We'll show the page now.
[00:07:58] Nadia: Opening the Alerts page — here's a sample alert for "project X usage > 80% of tokens/min" with an action to open a runbook or call a webhook.
[00:08:10] Dr. Karen Li: For pilot we need to know realistic default quotas so we can size our infra. What are typical defaults?
[00:08:16] Liam: Defaults are conservative: e.g., 100 requests/min and 50k tokens/min for new orgs on hosted tier. We bump these based on usage and plan. For Dedicated we set guaranteed throughput. We'll include concrete numbers in the matrix.
[00:08:30] [00:08:40] Priya: Any hard limits on concurrent streaming connections?
[00:08:44] Nadia: There's a per-connection limit but it's generally high; if you have extreme concurrency requirements we recommend Dedicated or reserve burst credits.
[00:08:54] Mike: How do you measure burst credits? Are they time-windowed?
[00:08:58] Nadia: Burst credits are based on token-bucket tokens — you accumulate credits up to a cap and spend them on bursts; replenishment is time based.
[00:09:10] [00:09:30] Samir: Another operational feature: we expose per-key SLO dashboards so you can see latency percentiles by key and route which helps triage if a single tenant is getting degraded performance.
[00:09:43] Jorge: On encryption and key management, can audit logs be sent to our SIEM?
[00:09:47] Nadia: Yes, export hooks to S3, GCS, or SIEM via webhook integrations. We'll attach the architecture note.
[00:09:56] [00:10:10] Liam: Quick demo of API flow — here's a curl creating a request with Authorization: Bearer <project-key>. See response headers with x-rate-limit info.
[00:10:20] Priya: Does the SDK surface rate-limit headers automatically?
[00:10:24] Nadia: Our SDK surfaces them; the JS/Go clients return a RateLimit struct and backoff helpers. For retries we recommend exponential backoff with jitter.
[00:10:35] [00:10:50] Dr. Karen Li: Does Optimize require instrumenting more headers or tracers?
[00:10:54] Samir: Optimize uses existing telemetry — we sample requests and analyze token patterns. You can opt-in to more detailed traces via a tracing header but it's optional.
[00:11:05] Priya: For the pilot, we need an automated test to validate rate limiting behavior. Can you provide a test harness?
[00:11:11] Nadia: We have a simple benchmark script that can replay a workload and assert quota enforcement; we'll share it. For Dedicated customers we can run a benchmark against the reserved pool.
[00:11:22] [00:11:40] Liam: We'll also include a suggested pilot plan: week 0 onboarding + key setup, week 1 load test and Optimize report, week 2 small production traffic and monitoring fine-tune.
[00:11:52] Mike: Sounds good. One last question — can we programmatically change quotas via API for autoscaling scenarios?
[00:11:58] Nadia: Yes, quotas and keys are manageable via API; but for rapid autoscaling we recommend using routing policies and reserved capacity rather than constantly changing quotas.
[00:12:10] [00:12:30] Dr. Karen Li: Ok let's talk about edge cases: what if a tenant tries to circumvent limits by spinning up many short-lived keys?
[00:12:36] Samir: We have anti-abuse checks: org-level aggregate quotas and anomaly detection. If you see key proliferation we can lock down key issuance to admins and enforce SSO-based provisioning.
[00:12:48] Jorge: For SSO we're using Okta — SAML SSO?
[00:12:52] Liam: Yes, SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning supported. We'll send the Okta integration doc.
[00:12:58] [00:13:10] Nadia: Demo wrap-up — quick recap of Console steps to create org default, add a project, create keys, apply a key-level quota, and set up an alert.
[00:13:22] Priya: One follow-up — can route policies do model fallback only for certain error codes?
[00:13:27] Samir: Yes, you can define conditions (e.g., 5xx or 429) and fallback targets.
[00:13:33] [00:13:50] Liam: Let's open for any other questions.
[00:13:55] Mike: On billing — how granular are invoices? We need per-project line items.
[00:13:59] Liam: We provide per-project usage export; invoices can be mapped to those projects. For enterprise we can do consolidated billing with project line items.
[00:14:10] Priya: For performance testing, what's a recommended payload size for your benchmarks?
[00:14:14] Nadia: Depends. For summarization we typically test with 2–4k token inputs; we'll include sample scripts.
[00:14:22] Dr. Karen Li: Anything else from your side?
[00:14:25] Jorge: Security sign-off will depend on SOC2 evidence and the audit logs retention options.
[00:14:30] Liam: Noted. We'll send SOC2, encryption, KMS, and the audit log export options.
[00:14:36] [00:14:50] Nadia: Final practical note — rate limits are enforced at the edge so there is low latency checking; we also surface counters in the response so engineers can implement graceful retries.
[00:15:02] Liam: Okay, recap of next steps and action items, then we'll close. Thanks everyone.
[00:15:10] Dr. Karen Li: Thanks — that was super helpful.
[00:15:15] Mike: Appreciate it, talk soon.
[00:15:20] -- End of recording --

Notes: Transcript contains occasional mis-hearings; some acronyms spelled out in audio as letters (e.g., S-A-M-L). Console screenshots and quickstart links will be attached in follow-up email.
